item.title: BYU’s Keanu Tanuvasa reflects on being on both sides of the BYU-Utah rivalry
item.description: BYU defensive tackle Keanu Tanuvasa hugs coach Sione Po'uha after Texas Tech Red defeated BYU in the Big 12 championship game at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, on Saturday, Dec. 6, 2025. | Isaac Hale, Deseret News When defensive tackle Keanu Tanuvasa left the University of Utah to join rival BYU a few years ago, he famously said that he knew the move “was going to cause earthquakes” in Salt Lake City. Metaphorically, he wasn’t wrong. The bold decision captured headlines for months and spawned plenty of nasty exchanges between Cougar and Ute fans, while the native of Mission Viejo, California, stayed mostly above the fray. “I am not surprised that they’re (8-0) because that’s Morgan’s attitude. That’s coach Scalley’s way of life. He is a go-getter, and that man has one of the greatest spirits that I’ve been around in being ruthlessly the best version of himself.” Keanu Tanuvasa on Morgan Scalley and the Utes Tanuvasa got the first laugh in the rivalry, as he and his new BYU teammates defeated Utah 24-21 last year in Provo , BYU’s third-straight win in the series. But now the redshirt senior has to face the Utah faithful in all their glory, Saturday at 10 a.m. at Rice-Eccles Stadium. Speaking of things that rattle, what kind of reception does he expect from Utah fans? “Nothing but their best, which is their passion, their fire, everything that comes along with it,” he said Monday. “I was one of the biggest advocates for them when I was there. I loved their passion, their impact on the game because I felt that when they were behind me as a player. So I don’t expect anything different going back up there as an opposing player. I’m excited for their fire and their juice.” Making this week even more interesting and exciting for the 6-foot-4, 300-pound NFL prospect is that his wife, Zerin, is due to deliver their son “any day now” in Provo. Tanuvasa said he will have BYU defensive line coach Sione Po’uha and several trainers “on standby” with his phone during practices and they will alert him if he needs to run off the field and over to the hospital. Suffice it to say that the week is shaping up to be one of the most emotional and memorable weeks in Tanuvasa’s life. “I’m excited. I think Rice-Eccles is a phenomenal place to play. It is one of my favorite stadiums in the entire country, and so being back there (brings a) lot of excitement. They got a great team.” Tanuvasa said he knows Utah’s standout offensive line well. “They are a freaking great bunch of guys that give huge effort,” he said. “I’ve seen that since they were young players. … I think the game that we play is a boys’ game, and we have a lot of fun doing it. So, I am just excited to go line it up.” Tanuvasa appeared in 24 games at Utah and started in 19 of them, including the 2024 game that ended in heartbreaking fashion for the Utes when Jake Retzlaff drove BYU into field goal range in the final minute and Will Ferrin kicked a 44-yard field goal for the 22-21 Cougars victory. item.title: St. Andrew's volleyball sees historic season come up short in semifinal
item.description: St. Andrew's volleyball season has drawn to a close one step shy of a Class 2A championship appearance. The Scots fell to two-time state champ Trinity Catholic (12-25, 17-25, 25-22, 13-25) in the 2A semifinals at Polk State College in Winter Haven, Florida on Tuesday night, ending a historic season. It was the first-ever state semifinal appearance for St. Andrew's despite a season highlighted by the performances of underclassmen across the roster. "What makes this team so special is not just what they accomplished on the volleyball court, but the character, resilience, and determination they showed throughout the season," St. Andrew's head coach Jorge Rivera said. "These young ladies faced challenges, overcame adversity, and continued to believe in each other when things weren't easy." More: The Post's Girls Athlete of the Week: Vote on the best of Oct. 26 - 31 The Scots (19-8) did not go down without a fight against Trinity Catholic (25-5) on Tuesday, battling back after going down 0-2 to take the third set with a 25-22 victory. Ultimately, Trinity Catholic's Emily Reed proved difficult to manage, and the Scots often found themselves on the backfoot against the No. 9 ranked team in the state. St. Andrew's has had a season worthy of recognition after making the deepest postseason run in program history. The team will graduate five seniors, but just two ― Kiersten Rodholm and Madelynn Ortlieb ― were in the regular rotation, meaning this is a program that is set up to return the majority of its key playmakers. With three eighth graders, led by star hitter Luiza Queiroz with over 300 kills on the year, the Scots are poised for a future of success. Between district and regional playoff matches, St. Andrew's lost just a single set and that's a trend that Palm Beach County volleyball fans might see more of moving forward. "Winning both the district and regional championship is an incredible accomplishment and a testament to their hard work, dedication, and commitment to one another," Rivera said. "Our goal is to establish a tradition of excellence where success is not measured by one season, but by the standards we set, the relationships we build, and the legacy we leave for future generations of players," River continued. "These championships are an important step in that journey, but they are not the finish line. I couldn't be prouder of these young ladies." Alex Peterman is a high school sports reporter for The Palm Beach Post. item.description: The Ohio High School Athletic Association girls soccer tournament is now down to the regional finals after semifinals action on Nov. 3. A number of Greater Cincinnati teams are now just one win away from reaching the OHSAA state tournament. Ten regional semis in five divisions were played and both of Cincinnati's defending OHSAA state champs went down. Here are the division-by-division results from those games and what's on the horizon for the regional finalists. Division I girls soccer regional semifinal results During the intermission between regulation and sudden death overtime, Mason superintendent Jonathan Cooper expressed his desire for a goal in the first minute. Senior Hailey Hommel, who has a knack for scoring in quick fashion, brought that manifestation to fruition with a goal just 51 seconds into the extra period, giving the Comets a 2-1 win over Lebanon to advance to their second regional final in the last three seasons. "The message was, 'It just takes one.' We poured our confidence in them and believed that we could do it. We had so many chances in regular time and we were just trying to pour our confidence," Mason coach Sami Ratowski said. It was Hommel's ninth goal of the year and the third straight game where she found the back of the net. It's the second time this year she has scored in at least three straight games, also doing so against Colerain, Middletown, Fairfield and Walnut Hills in early September. Many of those goals have come on assists from senior Bella Anderson, who notched her 12th of the season on the game winning goal. "She forms such great bonds with the entire team. She's a really amazing captain, probably my favorite, and she really tries to connect with people on a deeper level," Hommel said. Mason took control of the game from the outset with long stretches of possession, but couldn't put many shots on frame. Lucy Wiethe broke the stalemate with a roller across the goal in the 24th minute, not long after she subbed in. But Lebanon, unbeaten in October with a goal differential of 27-4, wouldn't go quietly. The Warriors applied immediate pressure to open the second half, equalizing on a rocket from Maddie Wagers in the 43rd minute. In the rest of regulation, Lebanon earned a few corners and free kicks in dangerous positions, but the only real threat was an Anderson breakaway and head-on shot that was smothered by Warriors keeper Carly Lansing. Lebanon graduates 11 seniors in Lansing, Wagers, Abby Nisonger, Paige Hensley, Georgia Stokes, Ali Kerns, Maia Nelson, Brianna Michaels, Emma Smith, Teagan Pullen and Zoe Hauser. And with no one but a rookie goaltender to back him up, fans have been starting to worry. With every game he plays, though, that rookie goalie is beginning to look like the answer. Sebastian Cossa has won four of his five starts this season, including three in a row — most recently against the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday. His one loss was initially a concern. It came in his second game of the season, where he allowed three goals on eight shots before Vejmelka relieved him of his position 16 minutes in. But, just as he told the Deseret News he would , he didn’t let that weigh him down. “I feel like throughout my career, I’ve done a really good job of bouncing back and (I) expect nothing less,” he said after returning to Utah after that game in Boston. “The next game I get, (I’ll) go in with a good mindset and just play my game.” That’s exactly what he did. Although he started to slip in the third period of Utah’s Oct. 19 game against the Pittsburgh Penguins, he had one more save than the goalie at the other end of the rink. He did it again in his next start, this time in Pittsburgh, winning 4-3 in overtime. His win in Toronto, though, was his most important yet. It came on the heels of a tough Mammoth loss. Vejmelka allowed five goals to the previously struggling Philadelphia Flyers (and the team gave up an empty-netter), causing much unrest among Mammoth fans. They needed one of the goalies to step up, and that’s exactly what Cossa did. The Maple Leafs threw a healthy 29 shots at Cossa, and he stopped 27 of them. His teammates can almost always be counted on to score at least three goals in a given game, and they held up their end of the bargain to scrape out a win. item.title: College Football Playoff Rankings Raise Miami-Notre Dame Game Stakes
item.description: Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr leads the Irish against Miami on Saturday in a pivotal home game. Miami is No. 1 in the College Football Playoff rankings, while Notre Dame is No. 11. Miami is one of three undefeated teams in the Football Bowl Subdivision, while Notre Dame is 7-1. (Photo by Chris Gardner/Getty Images) Getty Images Saturday’s Notre Dame-Miami football game already had plenty of intrigue. It is the first time since 1988 that the teams have played when each is in the top five of the Associated Press poll. The Hurricanes are No. 1, while the Fighting Irish are No. 4, just like they were 38 years ago when Notre Dame pulled off a one point victory and ended up winning its last national title. But the initial College Football Playoff rankings released Tuesday night put even more significance on Saturday’s contest. The CFP selection committee has Miami first and Notre Dame 11th. If the Irish win, they would be in a prime position to earn a spot in the 12-team playoff. But if they lose, they would risk not getting a place in the field because of their weak schedule. Notre Dame (7-1) has only faced one team in the CFP’s top 25, losing 28-24 at No. 9 BYU last month. And after Miami, the Irish do not face another ranked team in their final three regular season games. “The committee is impressed by (the Irish’s) performance on both sides of the ball,” Hunter Yurachek, the CFP selection chair, told ESPN’s Rece Davis Tuesday night. “They are a very good football team. But when you look at Notre Dame’s schedule and the wins that they have versus the teams that are ahead of them, they don’t have that signature win right now.” In the first CFP rankings last year, Notre Dame was No. 10 and Miami was No. 18 even though the teams had the same records and the Hurricanes defeated the Irish by three points at home in the season opener. The Hurricanes trailed Notre Dame in each of the rankings until the last week when they received the final at-large berth. The selection committee justified the move by noting Miami’s win over the Irish, but Notre Dame athletics director Pete Bevacqua criticized the decision, noting that the program had “a collective feeling that we were all just punched in the stomach.” This year, Notre Dame is guaranteed a spot in the field if it finishes in the top 12, a provision that was negotiated before last season’s controversy. But with the way the initial rankings shook out, Saturday represents a must-win for the Irish, which entered the season No. 4 in the AP poll and with national title aspirations. Outside of the BYU loss, Notre Dame has dominated its opponents and leads the nation with a 27-point average scoring margin over Football Bowl Subdivision foes. Although the Irish have the 55th-toughest strength of schedule in the FBS, they are first in ESPN’s Football Power Index, which is a forward-looking metric. item.title: Hertl delivers late to lift Knights past Penguins 3-2
item.description: Pittsburgh Penguins left wing Nick Robertson (14) plays the puck against Vegas Golden Knights defenseman Brayden McNabb (3) and goaltender Adin Hill (33) during the first period at PPG Paints Arena. PITTSBURGH — Not that things were so bad the night before in Boston, but Vegas Golden Knights coach Ryan Craig decided to shake things up Tuesday against the Pittsburgh Penguins. He moved Brett Howden up with Jack Eichel and Mark Stone. Ivan Barbashev skated with William Karlsson and Mitch Marner. Trevor Connelly went back to the third line. Jonas Rondbjerg was out, Raphael Lavoie was in. And Carter Hart sat in favor of Adin Hill. With the Knights having dropped five of their last six contests and desperately in need of two points, Craig believed this was the best way to accomplish that. After all, it was the second of back-to-back games and since it was 80s Night, Craig must have been listening to REO Speedwagon’s “Roll With The Changes” prior to puck drop. Whatever works, right? The Knights responded the way their coach hoped. A Tomas Hertl power play goal in the first period had them playing from in front instead of chasing the game. Hill had a strong night in the Vegas net, stopping 23 of 25 shots and the penalty kill was stellar, particularly late in the third period when the Penguins had a 5-on-3 power play for 1:22 with defensemen Jeremy Lauzon and Brayden McNabb sitting in the penalty box. Connelly delivered on a breakaway in the third period to tie it 2-2, scoring for the second straight night. And Hertl won it with 32.8 seconds left as he teamed up with Mark Stone and Jack Eichel for the game-winner as the Knights were on a late power play and got a 3-2 win and a sweep of the season series with Pittsburgh. The Knights defeated the Penguins 6-2 at T-Mobile Arena on Oct. 17. “I describe it as a grind,” said Craig. “We got some big penalty kills. We got a couple of goals on the power play. Our goaltender battled. There was some desperation there and a little bit of luck. But we got through it. And we got three points so far on the (road) trip.” Mitch Marner’s assist on Hertl’s first goal gave him a point in 11 straight games and 16 on the season. Yet he only has two goals as part of those 16 points. Still, No. 93 is contributing offensively. “I’m just trying to do my thing,” Marner said. “Get the puck in my hands and try to make plays. item.description: Coming into this season, even Milan Momcilovic’s biggest believers knew he’d face tremendous pressure to live up to his hefty contract. Compensation aside, performing at a high level at a program like Kentucky Basketball has its own unique challenges without any added friction points. So, it was fair to watch closely and maybe even form a quick opinion on how Momcilovic looked early in his Wildcat career. So far, the Iowa State transfer has done nothing but meet those lofty expectations head-on. After his stellar performance in UK’s dominant season-opening win Tuesday night, it’s fair to say he’s moved into the “exceeds expectations” column, and he shows no signs of slowing down. It isn’t just the stats that impress, though they certainly did tonight. It’s the smooth way in which Momcilovic operates. He stays steady and composed no matter the circumstance, and that was on display again Tuesday night as he scorched the Manhattan defense from all over the floor. His offense can be so effective with minimal dribbling, translating to gorgeous hoop actions. Momcilovic would finish the game with 24 points and five rebounds. But it was his 6/9 performance from behind the arc that left fans drooling and fantasizing about what could be in Mark Pope’s third season. Those six triples were actually tied for the most a Kentucky player has ever made in his debut. Antonio Reeves also hit six from deep in a 2023 win over Howard. There’s also an unquantifiable metric when it comes to how Milan Momcilovic’s talents open things up for his teammates through his own facilitation, or forcing the defense to pay so much attention to him that others find themselves open. This is something that Pope and his staff are sure to tinker with throughout the year. In just 28 minutes of total play, Milan Momcilovic gave college basketball a quick reminder that he’s the best shooter in the sport, and that’s not changing this season with an address change to Lexington. Two two-loss SEC teams were ranked ahead of undefeated UCLA, a clear statement about strength of schedule in a conference that loves to talk about theirs. Associated Press , Head-to-head results mattered quite a bit for some teams, but not at all for others. item.title: Highest successful run chases in ODI cricket at Eden Park, Auckland: Full list of records
item.description: Highest successful run chases in ODI cricket at Eden Park, Auckland: Full list of records originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: New Zealand’s 340/5 against Australia in 2007 is Eden Park’s highest successful ODI chase. Grant Elliott’s penultimate-ball six sealed the 2015 World Cup semi-final chase against South Africa. India’s tied 314/9 is the highest second-innings score at Eden Park without a win. Highest successful run chases in ODIs at Eden Park, Auckland Eden Park has a long history of high-scoring one-day contests, and the list of its biggest chases is dominated by the home side, though a few visiting teams have left their own mark on it. CN takes a look at the records as India open their five-match ODI series in New Zealand at this venue on Wednesday, November 4. The Indian team has bitter memories of the ground, having lost a 307-run chase here to New Zealand in November 2022 and having tied a match in 2014 after falling just short of a 315-run target. The record book also holds a famous World Cup moment. New Zealand’s semi-final win over South Africa in March 2015 produced one of the most memorable endings in the tournament’s history, with Grant Elliott striking a six off the penultimate ball to settle the result under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method. MORE: Eden Park dimensions: Boundary sizes at Eden Park stadium in Auckland detailed Highest successful ODI run chases at Eden Park, Auckland: Top 10 list The ground’s biggest successful chase came on February 18, 2007, when New Zealand overhauled a target of 337 against Australia with five wickets and nearly two overs to spare. They took 48.4 overs to get there, scoring at almost seven runs an over, which was a very high rate for ODI cricket of that period. Two batters did most of the damage. Ross Taylor made 117 and Craig McMillan added 52, and between them they kept the required rate under control through the middle overs before the lower order finished the job. No team has gone past that total in a chase at the venue in the years since. The third spot on the list belongs to the 2015 World Cup semi-final, played on March 24, when New Zealand were set 298 under the DLS method after rain affected the match. They reached 299 for 6 in 42.5 overs, a win by four wickets, and the equation was settled only when Elliott hit a six off the penultimate ball of the chase. The result sent New Zealand into their first World Cup final, and the shot remains one of the best-known moments in the tournament’s history. Visiting teams have succeeded here more often than the leading figures suggest. Zimbabwe chased 274 for 9 in 48.4 overs against New Zealand on January 7, 2001, while Pakistan reached 264 for 6 on March 21, 1992 and 251 for 3 on March 11, 1989. The West Indies won with 234 for 7 on March 4, 2006, which is the smallest total in the top ten. MORE: Kohli’s record in Auckland: How the India talisman has performed at Eden Par

item.description: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins Oilers Getty Edmonton Oilers forward Ryan Nugent-Hopkins set a team record by skating in his 1,038th career game with the franchise on Tuesday night. On Tuesday, the Oilers legend passed Lowe for the team record in regular-season games played, and it’s a record that’s not lost on him, given how many incredible players have played in Edmonton over the years. “Definitely meant a lot to me & feel the love… It’s a big honour for me & very fortunate to hit this milestone with this team,” Nugent-Hopkins said. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins on his teammates surprising him with shirts & a video ahead of today's morning skate. @Enterprise | #LetsGoOilers pic.twitter.com/bpDtS3cxEn — Edmonton Oilers (@EdmontonOilers) November 3, 2026 Ryan Nugent-Hopkins NHL Career Since being taken first overall in 2011, Nugent-Hopkins has played in 1,038 games for Edmonton, scoring 294 goals and 811 points. This season, Nugent-Hopkins has played in six games for the Oilers, scoring 3 goals and 7 points for the team. He will look to add to that total on Tuesday night when he takes on the Devils in his record-setting game for Edmonton. item.title: Commanders Snag Seahawks Recently Released RB After Jadarian Price Move
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Jadarian Price #8 of the Seattle Seahawks rushes against Shemar Turner #95 of the Chicago Bears during the fourth quarter of the game at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Olivia Vanni/Getty Images) Getty The Washington Commanders took back the running back the Seattle Seahawks signed away from them less than a month ago. Washington claimed Robert Henry Jr. off waivers on Tuesday, Nov. 3, according to the NFL transaction wire. The Seahawks had waived the undrafted rookie a day earlier to open a spot on the 53-man roster for first-round pick Jadarian Price, who was activated from injured reserve before Monday night’s game against the Chicago Bears. Had Henry cleared waivers, Seattle would have been free to offer him a spot on its practice squad. The Commanders’ claim took that option off the table and put Henry on Washington’s active roster. Commanders Get Robert Henry Jr. Back From Seahawks Washington was Henry’s first NFL team. The Commanders signed him after the draft out of UTSA, gave him 26 preseason carries and brought him back on the practice squad after final cuts. He ran for 105 yards and a touchdown in three preseason games. Seattle signed Henry off that practice squad on Oct. 6, when Price was on injured reserve and Zach Charbonnet was still working his way back from a torn ACL. The Seahawks had started Emanuel Wilson against the Los Angeles Chargers two days earlier. They added Henry to the active roster and signed Dontae McMillan to the practice squad in the same round of moves. Henry had some burst worth a look. In his final season at UTSA, he rushed for 1,045 yards and nine touchdowns on 151 carries, averaging 6.9 yards per attempt. Five of his runs went for at least 70 yards. Washington had already seen some of that speed in an NFL uniform when Henry scored on a 22-yard run against Miami in August. Jadarian Price’s Return Changed Seattle’s Backfield The Seahawks confirmed Monday that they waived Henry to make room for Price. The rookie from Notre Dame missed four games with a chest injury after rushing for 119 yards on 28 carries in his first three NFL games. He also caught four passes for 21 yards. Price’s activation came as Charbonnet returned for his season debut against Chicago. That was a different backfield from the one Henry joined in October, when the Seahawks needed healthy runners behind Wilson and had no immediate return date for either Price or Charbonnet. Washington had its own reason to move quickly. As Heavy reported , the Commanders were dealing with an injury to Jacory Croskey-Merritt. The waiver wire gave them a chance to fill a need with a player they’d already evaluated through a full training camp and preseason. In October, Seattle had the active-roster opening that got Henry out of Washington. When that spot went back to Price, the Commanders used theirs to get Henry back. item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. He didn’t know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance. “They didn’t ask much of me,” Comer said. “They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback.” What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability.
